nodes.label: Seven-Layer Model
nodes.rationale: The book's organizing frame: every ZK system decomposes into seven layers (setup, language, witness, arithmetization, proof system, primitives, verification). The author presents it as a pedagogical map that is deliberately provisional -- by Chapter 10 it is redrawn as a DAG with fourteen causal edges because real systems fuse and invert the layer boundaries.

nodes.label: 4x4 Sudoku Running Example
nodes.rationale: Chosen because it is small enough to hold in your head, complex enough to exercise every layer (range checks, uniqueness, boundaries), and needs no math background; it is traced through Chapters 3-6 as program, witness, 72-96 constraints, and sealed proof.

nodes.label: Trust-Minimized (vs Trustless)
nodes.rationale: The book's central thesis: 'trustless' is marketing; ZK proofs do not eliminate trust but decompose one monolithic assumption into seven independent, weaker, testable ones. The author deliberately adopts the uglier word because it is accurate.

nodes.label: Capex/Opex Setup Economics Framework
nodes.rationale: Author's lens for why trusted setups persist: the ceremony is a one-time capital expenditure amortized across every circuit, while per-proof verification is operating expense -- the argument for ceremonies is economic, not philosophical.

nodes.label: Quantum Shelf Life of Trusted Setups
Four Layer-2 Language Philosophies
nodes.rationale: The taxonomy (EVM-compatible, ZK-native ISA, general-purpose ISA, application-specific DSL) is framed around what the developer sees, because what the developer sees determines what bugs they make -- and bugs, not cryptographic breaks, are the largest source of real-world ZK failures.

nodes.label: The Witness Gap (50-70% of proving time)
Privacy as a Luxury Good
nodes.rationale: The hardware ladder argument: client-side proving (maximum privacy) demands hardware most of the world does not own, so over 90% of people must delegate proving and trust a service with their secrets -- the technical Memory Gap becomes a political equity problem.

nodes.label: Hybrid STARK-to-SNARK Pipeline
nodes.rationale: The dominant 2026 production pattern: a transparent STARK inner proof (no ceremony, post-quantum) recursively compressed and wrapped in Groth16 for cheap on-chain verification. The SNARK-vs-STARK debate was a false dichotomy; Ethereum gas economics forced 'STARK inside, SNARK outside'.

nodes.label: Cryptographic Primitives Trilemma
nodes.rationale: The author's own framing (explicitly not from the literature): a commitment scheme achieves at most two of algebraic functionality, post-quantum security, and succinctness. Presented as a historical snapshot being actively dissolved by the lattice folding line, not a permanent law.

nodes.label: BN254 Curve (~100-bit security after Tower NFS)
The Cascade Effect / One-Way Door
nodes.rationale: Layer 6 field choice cascades upward with algebraic necessity -- field determines commitment scheme, which determines proof system, which determines arithmetization -- so 'crypto-agility' is largely fiction for ZK systems; changing the field is a full redesign.

nodes.label: Midnight
nodes.rationale: Chosen as the book's full-stack running case study because the author founded IOG, the company that built it, giving access to internal architecture at unusual depth; the author flags the bias and designs Chapter 12's claims to be independently verifiable. Framed as a 'privacy theater' where ZK proofs are the execution model itself, not an optimization.
